# Constraints

## Edge shapes

| Type | From | To | Hint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| motivates | purpose | outcome | Is the reason the target exists (purpose → outcome). |
| serves | capability, feature | audience, goal, outcome | Delivers value to an audience. |
| satisfies | capability, feature | problem, usecase | Meets a problem-space statement. |
| has | audience, capability, feature, problem | agent, context, flow, problem, usecase | Conceptual possession (audience has problem). |
| implements | agent, flow, screen | capability, feature, task | Realises a solution-space spec. |
| contains | codebase, epic, module, repository, system | ai-function, asset, codebase, event, infra, module, protocol, rule, task, test, thing | Composition (screen contains component). |
| exposes | module | interface, screen | Module exposes an interface. |
| emits | interface | event | Produces an event (interface or rule emits event). |
| combines | goal | metric | Goal combines metrics. |
| measures | feedback, metric-reading, usage-event | flow, metric, screen | Metric reading measures a metric; usage events and feedback measure an outcome or feature. |
| targets | epic, task | test | Task or epic targets the tests it must turn green. |
| reports | test-result | test | Test result reports on a test (reality → representation). |
| realises | codebase, infrastructure, practice | infra, module, protocol, system | Actual code realises a solution-space module or item (current state → solution). |
| governs | practice, rule | codebase, thing | Rule governs a thing (or several: relationship rules). |
| defines | term | event, module, thing | Glossary term defines a node. |
| uses | ai-function, audience, codebase, external, flow, infra, interface, module, protocol, screen, system | external, infra, infrastructure, interface, module, screen, system, thing | Runtime dependency. |
| references | assumption, capability, event, flow, goal, hypothesis, screen | capability, flow, hypothesis, metric, outcome, problem, test, thing | Weak link of last resort. |
| triggers | event, module | event, module | Causal succession. |
| verifies | test | rule | Test verifies a rule (one per condition). |
| monitors | metric | outcome | Metric watches an outcome. |
| supports | evidence | hypothesis | Evidence supports a hypothesis. STUB. |
| refutes | evidence | hypothesis | Evidence refutes a hypothesis. STUB. |
| in-stage | any | any | Tags any node with a lifecycle stage. |
| carries | interface | thing | Interface carries a payload that is or derives from this thing ("molecules" entering/leaving through the interface's in/out). |
| hosts | infra | module | Deployable (infra) hosts a module, at the deployment level. Additional to `contains` (module → infra), which the Modules grid still reads — do not repurpose that one. |

## Kinds and their structural needs

| Kind | Edge | Direction | Min | What to ask |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| hypothesis | references | out | 1 | How would you know "{title}" holds? Name one metric. |
| module | exposes | out | 1 | What does "{title}" expose to the rest of the system? Name its interface. |
| rule | verifies | in | 1 | How would we know "{title}" holds? One test per line, naming the condition. |
| protocol | realises | in | 1 | What practice realises "{title}" today, or is this a planned change? |
| test | verifies | out | 1 | Which rule does "{title}" verify? |
| task | targets | out | 1 | Which test(s) must "{title}" turn green? |

## Invariants

| Id | Text | Raise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| inv-commit-gate | A node or edge becomes committed only through a Commit. Agents never write directly; their output is a changeset. | — |
| inv-provenance | Every effect traces to exactly one Answer or one Action. | — |
| inv-kernel-additive | Templates can add kinds, edge types, and questions; they cannot remove kernel ones. | — |
| inv-unlock | A question unlocks only after all of its unlocksAfter questions have a committed answer. | — |
| inv-undo | Undo reverts one whole Commit, never a partial. | — |
| inv-left-to-right | Spaces are enriched left to right: basics → problem → hypothesis → solution. | — |
| inv-fixed-vocab | Once a term is committed in the vocabulary, other nodes should use it verbatim. | — |
| inv-code-ref | Every level-3 item may carry props.codeRef, a URL to the file or block on GitHub that implements it. | — |
| inv-rule-has-test | Every rule has at least one test per condition; tests are how the representation connects to reality. | `question` |
| inv-green-means-done | If every test result is pass, there are no planned changes. Any fail or missing result must be targeted by a task. | `task` |
| inv-test-ladder | Tests climb a ladder: a basic existence check first, for every module including business ones → its API surface → deterministic simulation. | — |
| inv-protocol-realised | Every protocol in the representation is realised by a practice in reality, or its absence is a planned change. | `question` |
| inv-module-boundary | Modules keep boundaries strict enough to be tested by deterministic simulation. | — |
| inv-whole-business | Modules, tests and effects cover every aspect of the business — promotion, sales, marketing, delivery, implementation — not just the tech product. | — |
| inv-one-utterance | The mirror shows at most one utterance (or one question) at a time. | — |
| inv-agent-through-gate | Agent data changes go through the commit gate like everyone else's; only glossary edits take the escape hatch. | — |
| inv-dogfood | Bropilot must be describable in Bropilot with no special cases. | — |
| inv-edits-are-effects | Edits are effects too, not just new nodes: an update-node effect goes through the same commit gate as an add-node one. | — |
| inv-meta-relation-rules | Rules exist at the meta level as well as the node level: relations between nodes are governed by kernel rules (edge shape, needs), same as nodes encode domain rules. | — |
| inv-edge-shape | Every edge fits the declared from/to kinds of its edge type. | `question` |
| inv-needs-cardinality | A kind's `needs` are structural expectations on its instances: at least `min` edges of the named type and direction. | `question` |
| inv-test-has-rule | A codebase test ties an expectation of the representation to reality: every test verifies a rule. | `question` |
| inv-meta-tests-raise-questions | The meta level is tested too: where the kernel is not followed, the check raises a question or clarification request for the user, never a silent auto-repair. | `question` |
| inv-one-test-kind | There is one test kind; `resultSource` (code, metric, manual) varies, not the kind. | — |
| inv-staleness-cascade | Staleness on edit is transitive, with an early cutoff: a neighbour revalidated unchanged clears its edges and stops the spread; a neighbour that was itself edited cascades again. | — |
| inv-condition-one-line | A rule's condition is one line of its description text (or its title, if it has none). | — |
| inv-suspect-pending | A suspect edge stays surfaced until the node it touches is revalidated. | `question` |
| inv-reviewer-gate | A task is done only after its full suite is green and a reviewer agent verdict, not on green tests alone. | — |
